title: S1-07 Spike - catalogue every unpersisted write

input.requestedOutcome: Produce a ranked catalogue (mutation site / store / persisted? / lost on reload?) of every place in allotment_v2.html that mutates a data store but never reaches a persistence call, going beyond the four documented instances named in the ticket (aosSaveModal/SB_ADDON_SVCS, ctRenewActivate, flSaveAssignment/flCancelAssignment/flAutoUpdateAssignments, fuelSetBudget).
acceptanceCriteria: Deliverable is a document only; allotment_v2/allotment_v2.html and every other source file are read-only for this task
All four named sites (SB_ADDON_SVCS/aosSaveModal, ctRenewActivate, flSaveAssignment/flCancelAssignment/flAutoUpdateAssignments, fuelSetBudget) are verified directly against source and included
At least one additional unpersisted-write instance beyond the four named sites is found via systematic search and verified
Output is a ranked table (mutation site / store / persisted? / lost on reload?) ordered by blast radius
Every claim in the catalogue is backed by a specific line reference read from the actual function body, not inferred from ticket text alone
constraints: Must not modify allotment_v2/allotment_v2.html or any other source file — read-only spike
Must not touch files owned by other in-flight tasks
Stage only the three owned paths explicitly; never git add -A / git add .
assumptions: No Postgres instance or prod service is reachable from this sandbox, so DB-round-trip claims (row 4, fleet_fuelbudget) are verified statically via field_mapping.json/operation_schemas_model.json/server.js logic, not by a live reproduction
The line numbers in allotment_v2.html cited throughout are current as of commit fa60a96 on this branch and will drift; the catalogue itself says to grep the function name instead

output.summary: Delivered docs/development/unpersisted-writes.md: a 7-row ranked catalogue of mutation sites in allotment_v2.html that never reach (or only conditionally reach) a persistence call. Verified all four Jira-named sites directly against current source, corrected two ticket assumptions after reading the code (flSaveAssignment/flCancelAssignment/flAutoUpdateAssignments and fuelSetBudget DO call localStorage.setItem directly — the real defects are a missing laCanEditArea('fleet') permission guard and, for fuelSetBudget, a completely unregistered blob key on the relational backend), found one previously-undocumented sibling bug (aosDeleteService also mutates SB_AGENTS[].addonServices without sbAgentsPersist()), and surfaced three more instances (accounting/booking edit-area guard mismatch, an OCR-failure branch that never persists, and SB_AGENT_PRICES's boot-only regeneration) by systematically grepping all eight allotment_v2/docs/workflows/*.md files for prior persistence-gap language and re-verifying each against current source rather than trusting the doc text. No source file was modified.

decisions: Classified the raw ~170 hits of a blind `grep localStorage.setItem` as mostly NOT bugs: this codebase's actual persistence pattern is direct read-modify-write of the LS_KEY blob (verified via the Storage.prototype.setItem override at allotment_v2.html:64-82, which auto-syncs any write to that key to /api/save), not a mandatory single save() call. Only mutation sites with zero or conditional reach to that write were catalogued.

Corrected two of the ticket's four named sites after reading the code: flSaveAssignment/flCancelAssignment/flAutoUpdateAssignments and fuelSetBudget DO call localStorage.setItem(LS_KEY,...) directly, contrary to a literal 'never persist' reading — the real, verified defects are a missing laCanEditArea('fleet') guard on all four, an `if(ls.boats)` conditional on the first three, and (new finding) fuelSetBudget's fleet_fuelbudget key having zero server-side relational mapping.

Used the existing docs/workflows/*.md corpus as a search accelerator (grep for prior 'not persisted' language) rather than scanning all ~600 top-level functions in the 83k-line file by hand, given the spike's effort budget — every candidate surfaced this way was independently re-verified against current source before inclusion, not copied from the docs as-is.
risks: Row 4 (fleet_fuelbudget) is verified statically only; without a reachable Postgres/prod instance this task cannot prove the round-trip loss happens at runtime, only that the code path for it to happen is present and unguarded.

Line numbers throughout the catalogue will drift as the file is edited by other in-flight tasks; the document tells readers to grep the function name, but a stale-line complaint should not be read as the catalogue being wrong.

The catalogue is not exhaustive — it covers the four named sites plus every additional instance found via the doc-grep sweep and direct reading of the immediately adjacent code; a full line-by-line audit of all ~600 top-level functions in the 83k-line file was out of scope for a spike-level effort budget.
followUps: A future fix task should: add sbAgentsPersist() to ctRenewActivate; load/persist SB_ADDON_SVCS like every other SB_* list and add sbAgentsPersist() to aosDeleteService's SB_AGENTS side-effect; add the missing laCanEditArea('fleet') guard to flSaveAssignment/flCancelAssignment/flAutoUpdateAssignments/fuelSetBudget; register fleet_fuelbudget in field_mapping.json + operation_schemas_model.json; align the acctPersistBookings/sbInvoicesPersist edit-area guards; add a persist call to the OCR failure branch. (Listed in docs/development/unpersisted-writes.md §4.)

Consider a follow-up spike or lint rule that flags any top-level function mutating a global SB_*/FL_* array without a same-function call to a *Persist()/save()/flSave() helper, to catch future instances of this bug class automatically.
rollback: Revert this commit (or delete docs/development/unpersisted-writes.md, docs/development/tasks/LAM-21.md, and .agent-reports/LAM-21.json) — the task added only new documentation files and touched no runtime code, so rollback has zero effect on application behavior or data.
